fields.headline:
2.1
Vectors & Vector Basics
fields.subhead: Recall what a vector is, how to draw one, and how to describe its direction — before we add them together.

imageSubjects.section: a wooden protractor and ruler laid across graph paper

fields.headline: Quick Recall: Vector Vocabulary
fields.subhead: You built all of this in Unit 1. Here's the short version.
fields.k1_b:
Has magnitude AND direction.
Drawn as an arrow.
fields.k2_b:
The size or length.
Always positive.
fields.k3_b:
A vector's x- or y-part.
A cos(theta), A sin(theta).
fields.mustwrite: A vector needs both magnitude and direction — a number alone is not one.

imageSubjects.aside: a compass rose drawn in pencil on aged paper

fields.headline: Drawing and Resolving, Recap
fields.subhead: Two skills from Unit 1, Section 1.0 — you should already be comfortable with both.
fields.c1_b:
Arrow length = magnitude.
Arrow direction = angle.
Tip points the way it acts.
fields.c2_b:
x-part: A cos(theta)
y-part: A sin(theta)
Right-triangle trig.
fields.mustwrite: Full walkthrough and practice: Unit 1, Section 1.0.
